Routine Descriptions

SRSCAN_API_CONFIG

 [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  srscan_api_config

PURPOSE:
  Central configuration for the srs_canada data loading path. All
  dataset names, endpoints, and cache conventions used by the srscan_*
  routines live here so that product/dataset changes are one-line edits.

  The API base URL can be overridden with the SRSCAN_API_URL
  environment variable (useful for testing against staging servers);
  the HAPI server URL (hapi_url) follows the same host.

OUTPUT:
  Structure of configuration constants.

NOTES:
  Data documentation: https://data.phys.ucalgary.ca
  API documentation:  https://api.phys.ucalgary.ca

  Data files are cached under !srs_canada.local_data_dir + <DATASET_NAME>,
  mirroring the archive tree below each dataset's data_tree_url.

SRSCAN_DEDUP_GZ

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  srscan_dedup_gz

PURPOSE:
  Some archive trees (notably stream2 summary products) contain
  BOTH an uncompressed file and its gzipped twin, and the data
  distribution API lists both. Downloading/reading both wastes transfer
  and duplicates every data record. This function reduces a list of URLs
  or file paths to one entry per logical file, PREFERRING the .gz
  variant; entries that only exist uncompressed are kept as-is.

INPUT:
  files: string array of URLs or paths

OUTPUT:
  Filtered string array (original order preserved).

(See projects/srs_canada/api/srscan_dedup_gz.pro)

SRSCAN_DOWNLOAD

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  srscan_download

PURPOSE:
  Download data files from the data archive (data.phys.ucalgary.ca) for
  a given dataset, timeframe, and optional site. File URLs are resolved
  with srscan_get_urls (the api.phys.ucalgary.ca data distribution
  endpoint) and fetched with the standard SPEDAS spd_download, so
  proxy/network behavior matches the rest of SPEDAS.

  Files are cached under
    !srs_canada.local_data_dir + '<DATASET_NAME>/<archive tree>'
  mirroring the archive layout below the dataset's data_tree_url.
  Files already present in the cache are not re-downloaded (the archive
  files are immutable).

INPUT:
  dataset_name: dataset to download, e.g. 'TREX_RGB_RAW_NOMINAL' (string)
  start_ts:     start timestamp, ISO format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS (string)
  end_ts:       end timestamp (inclusive), same format (string)

KEYWORDS:
  site_uid:    4-letter site UID filter, e.g. 'gill' (string)
  device_uid:  device UID filter, e.g. 'rgb-04' (string)
  no_download: if set, do not contact the API or server at all; returns
               count=0 (callers fall back to globbing the local cache)
  verbose:     dprint verbosity passthrough

OUTPUT:
  Structure:
    { files:     string array of local absolute paths (only files that
                 exist locally after the call),
      count:     number of elements in files,
      relpaths:  archive-tree-relative paths (below data_tree_url),
      data_tree_url: the dataset's archive root URL,
      total_urls: number of URLs the API listed,
      api_ok:    1b if the API responded (even with zero URLs), 0b if the
                 API was not contacted or the request failed }
  Returns count=0 structure if nothing was listed/downloaded.

EXAMPLE:
  d = srscan_download('TREX_RGB_RAW_NOMINAL', $
        '2023-03-24T06:00:00','2023-03-24T06:59:59', site_uid='gill')

(See projects/srs_canada/api/srscan_download.pro)

SRSCAN_FILES_IN_WINDOW

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  srscan_files_in_window

PURPOSE:
  Filter a list of archive file paths to those whose filename start
  timestamp lies within [t0, t1] -- the same "file START time in
  [start, end]" rule the data distribution API applies to listings, so
  the offline cache-glob fallbacks resolve the same file set the server
  query would.

  Without this, the hour globs can catch granules far outside the
  request window: a single-frame time= request globs every minute file
  of the hour (~60x the data needed -- ~1 GB of raw frames, or ~7.5 GB
  of MOSv001 grids, to keep one frame).

  Archive basenames start 'YYYYMMDD_hhmm_' (minute granules) or
  'YYYYMMDD_hh_' (hour granules); files whose basename does not match
  either form are kept (fail open).

INPUT:
  files:  string array of file paths
  t0, t1: window bounds (unix time, inclusive)

KEYWORDS:
  count: (out) number of files kept

OUTPUT:
  Filtered string array ('' when count is 0; original order preserved).

(See projects/srs_canada/api/srscan_files_in_window.pro)

SRSCAN_GET_URLS

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  srscan_get_urls

PURPOSE:
  Retrieve the URLs of files available for download from the data
  archive for a given dataset, timeframe, and optional site.
  This is the file-listing step of the srs_canada loading path; the file
  GETs themselves are done by srscan_download.

INPUT:
  dataset_name: dataset to list, e.g. 'TREX_RGB_RAW_NOMINAL' (string)
  start_ts:     start timestamp, ISO format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS (string)
  end_ts:       end timestamp (inclusive), same format (string)

KEYWORDS:
  site_uid:   4-letter site UID to filter on, e.g. 'gill' (string)
  device_uid: device UID to filter on, e.g. 'rgb-04' (string)
  verbose:    dprint verbosity passthrough

OUTPUT:
  Structure with tags urls (list of full https URLs), count, path_prefix,
  and dataset (struct with data_tree_url etc.), as returned by the API.
  Returns !null on any request/parse failure.

EXAMPLE:
  u = srscan_get_urls('TREX_RGB_RAW_NOMINAL', $
        '2023-03-24T06:00:00','2023-03-24T06:59:59', site_uid='gill')

NOTES:
  Proxies are resolved by srscan_proxy, so a proxy configured the
  usual SPEDAS way works here with no extra setup:
    setenv, 'http_proxy=http://proxy.example.org:3128'

(See projects/srs_canada/api/srscan_get_urls.pro)

SRSCAN_PROXY

 [Previous Routine] [Next Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  srscan_proxy

PURPOSE:
  Resolve the HTTP proxy configuration to use for srs_canada data
  traffic, returned with IDLnetURL property names so the result
  can be applied directly with IDLnetURL::SetProperty or handed to
  spd_download through _extra.

  This exists so that the API listing call (srscan_get_urls,
  which drives its own IDLnetURL object) obeys the same proxy settings as
  the file downloads, which go through spd_download and therefore already
  pick up http_proxy inside spd_download_file.

  Resolution order:
    1. AURORAX_PROXY_HOSTNAME and AURORAX_PROXY_PORT (with optional
       AURORAX_PROXY_USERNAME / AURORAX_PROXY_PASSWORD). This is the
       idl-aurorax convention, kept so existing setups keep working, and
       treated as an override because it is the more specific setting.
    2. http_proxy, the standard SPEDAS convention, parsed by spd_get_proxy
       -- the exact call spd_download_file makes -- so a proxy configured
       the usual SPEDAS way needs no extra setup here:
         setenv, 'http_proxy=http://user:pass@proxy.example.org:3128'

KEYWORDS:
  verbose: dprint verbosity passthrough

OUTPUT:
  Structure with proxy_hostname, proxy_port, proxy_username and
  proxy_password tags, or !null when no proxy is configured. Passing an
  undefined/!null value through _extra is a no-op in IDL, so callers can
  forward the result unconditionally.

NOTES:
  spd_get_proxy leaves its argument undefined when http_proxy is unset or
  unparseable, which is what makes the !null return work.

(See projects/srs_canada/api/srscan_proxy.pro)

SRSCAN_SKYMAP

 [Previous Routine] [List of Routines] 
FUNCTION:
  srscan_skymap

PURPOSE:
  Locate, download, and restore the best skymap for a site at a
  given time: the skymap with the latest validity start time at or before
  the requested time. If the requested time predates all available
  skymaps, the earliest one is used with a warning.

  This routine is instrument-agnostic: the skymap dataset is passed in,
  so every srs_canada imager network reuses it unmodified (e.g.
  'TREX_RGB_SKYMAP_IDLSAV', and in the future 'TREX_NIR_SKYMAP_IDLSAV',
  'SMILE_ASI_SKYMAP_IDLSAV', ...).

INPUT:
  dataset_name: skymap dataset, e.g. 'TREX_RGB_SKYMAP_IDLSAV' (string)
  site:         4-letter site code, e.g. 'gill' (string)
  time:         requested time (double unix time or string)

KEYWORDS:
  no_download: use only the local cache
  verbose:     dprint verbosity
  filename:    (out) local path of the restored skymap file

OUTPUT:
  the restored skymap structure, or -1 if none could be obtained

(See projects/srs_canada/api/srscan_skymap.pro)
